product: Goal Zero Yeti 1500X Portable Power Station (1516Wh, 2000W)

price_today.value: Amazon price not read from a confirmed seller. amzcheck showed $1,499.95 on B0HP944GSP, but Amazon returned 503 on the product page, so the seller is unknown and we should not link it.

wins.need: Running 12V gear that draws a lot of current (fridges, compressors, winches) straight from DC
wins.claim: Has a 12V Anderson power-pole output rated 30A / 360W, plus a 12V car port (13A / 160W) and a 6mm port (10A / 120W). I could not read rivals' 12V ratings, so this is a spec, not a proven win over any named model.
wins.who: Goal Zero Yeti 1500X user guide, technical specifications

wins.need: Short loads a little above the rated 2000W
wins.claim: In MakeUseOf's test it held a load above its continuous rating without shutting off. No rival was tested the same way.
wins.figure: About 2,250W (1,800W hairdryer plus 900W steamer) for about 6 minutes without tripping overload protection (Matt L. Hall, MakeUseOf, 25 May 2021)

wins.need: Lighter than Goal Zero's own replacement model
wins.claim: Lighter than the new LiFePO4 Yeti 1500 (arithmetic: 52.75 − 45.64 = about 7.1 lb lighter). It is still about 13.7 lb heavier than the Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 (31.97 lb).
wins.figure: 45.64 lb (MakeUseOf spec) vs 52.75 lb for the new Yeti 1500 (goalzero.com store data)
wins.who: MakeUseOf spec list; Goal Zero store listing read with storecheck

wins.need: Fast charging, but only with a separately sold charger
wins.claim: With Goal Zero's Yeti X 600W Power Supply ($249.95, sold separately) it fully charges in 3 hours. The included 120W charger is far slower (see weak).
wins.figure: 3 hours with the 600W supply (Goal Zero accessory page); MakeUseOf saw about 3 hours at the 600W input
wins.who: Goal Zero accessory listing (storecheck); Matt L. Hall, MakeUseOf

weak.claim: Older NMC battery rated for far fewer full cycles than LiFePO4 rivals
weak.figure: 500 cycles to 80% (Li-ion NMC, from the user guide) vs Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 at 6,000+ cycles and EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max at 3,000+ cycles (maker store pages)

weak.claim: Very slow to charge from the wall with the included charger
weak.figure: User guide: 10 hrs with the 120W wall charger. Offgridweb (Patrick McCarthy, 14 Oct 2024): about 14 hrs. MakeUseOf: about 13 hrs. Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 claims 0–100% in 64 minutes.

weak.claim: Costs far more per Wh than current rivals at the Amazon price seen (arithmetic)
weak.figure: $1,499.95 for 1,516Wh (unconfirmed Amazon listing) vs Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 at $849 for 1,536Wh. The 1500X costs about $651 more for 20Wh less. It also matches the $1,499.95 price of Goal Zero's newer LiFePO4 Yeti 1500.
MakeUseOf lists 'only two AC ports' as a con. Jackery 1500 v2 has 3 AC outlets and EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max has 6 (maker pages).

weak.claim: Reliability problems with the review unit
weak.figure: Offgridweb: the included charger overheated and melted through the lid tray after about 90 minutes on the first charge, and the unit was replaced under warranty. The 12V port also tripped on an 8A air-mattress pump.

weak.claim: Inverter draws power while idle, and the battery needs topping up in storage
weak.figure: AC inverter draws 7W with nothing plugged in (yuenx review, 4 Jan 2021). Shelf life: charge every 3–6 months (user guide).
24 months (MakeUseOf spec list) vs 5 years on the new Yeti 1500 (Goal Zero store)

wins_for: Owners who already have Goal Zero Anderson/HPP solar panels or a Yeti Home Integration Kit (listed as needing a Yeti 1000X or larger) and can get a 1500X well below the price of current LiFePO4 models
Shoppers who need a high-current 12V Anderson output (360W) and accept a 500-cycle battery
not_for: Anyone paying about $1,500. The new Goal Zero Yeti 1500 costs the same ($1,499.95) and has LiFePO4 cells, 1500W AC fast charging and a 5-year warranty.
Shoppers who care about value per Wh. The Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 ($849, 1,536Wh, 6,000+ cycles, 31.97 lb) wins.
Home backup with lots of outlets or room to add batteries. The EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max ($1,029, 6 AC outlets, expands to 6kWh, 3,000+ cycles) wins.
Daily cycling or long service life. Any LiFePO4 rival wins over its 500-cycle NMC pack.
Carrying it around (45.6 lb, and Offgridweb and MakeUseOf both flag the weight). The Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 at 31.97 lb wins.

rivals.where_it_beats_ours: LiFePO4 cells; 1500W AC fast charge vs a 120W included charger; 900W combined solar vs 600W; 405W 12V HPP vs 360W; 260W combined USB-C; IPX4; 5-year warranty. It is 7.1 lb heavier (52.75 lb).
1,536Wh LiFePO4 with 6,000+ cycles; 4000W surge vs 3500W; 3 AC outlets; 64-minute full charge; 31.97 lb; about $651 cheaper
LFP with 3,000+ cycles; expands from 2kWh to 6kWh; 6 AC outlets; X-Boost up to 3400W; up to 1000W solar input
2,042Wh LFP; 2200W continuous / 4400W surge; under 20ms switchover; 0–100% in about 1.7 h; about 39.5 lb; about 95% charge kept after 12 months in storage

targets.headline: Goal Zero power stations: should you buy the new model or the older one still for sale?
targets.why_it_wins_there: It doesn't win; the page should feature the new LiFePO4 Yeti 1500. The 1500X belongs there only as the older model shoppers will still see listed. At the same $1,499.95, the new model has 1500W AC charging vs 120W, LiFePO4 vs 500-cycle NMC, and a 5-year vs 2-year warranty (goalzero.com store data; Yeti 1500X user guide; MakeUseOf). No search with volume fits a page that features the 1500X as a pick.

record.summary: An older 1516Wh NMC power station with a 2000W inverter and a high-current 12V Anderson output, now replaced by Goal Zero's LiFePO4 Yeti 1500.
record.fit: Goal Zero owners with Anderson/HPP solar gear or a Home Integration Kit who find it at a deep discount; not a first pick at full price.
caveats: 500-cycle NMC battery vs 3,000–6,000+ cycles on LiFePO4 rivals (user guide; Jackery and EcoFlow store pages)
Included 120W charger takes 10 hrs per the user guide, about 14 hrs per Offgridweb
45.6 lb with only two AC outlets (MakeUseOf)
Offgridweb's first unit's charger overheated and melted the lid tray; replaced under warranty
Inverter draws 7W idle (yuenx); recharge every 3–6 months in storage (user guide)

unsourced: Amazon seller: amzcheck found B0HP944GSP ('GOAL ZERO YETI 1500X PORTABLE POWER STATION', $1,499.95, 13 ratings) and B0HMQ5VGN4 ('YETI 1500X Portable Power Station', $289, 11,394 ratings). The $289 price with that many ratings looks wrong for this product and suggests a reused or merged listing. Both Amazon pages returned HTTP 503 to WebFetch and curl was blocked, so I could not read Ships from or Sold by for either. asin is null.

Goal Zero's own Yeti 1500X page and the 1500X expansion-system page returned HTTP 429 every time I tried. A Goal Zero store search for '1500X' and 'Yeti 1500X' on 2026-11-15 showed no 1500X listing, only the new Yeti 1500 and accessories. I could not confirm whether the 1500X is discontinued, its official warranty, or its official weight and dimensions.
Measured usable capacity (Wh delivered) and efficiency: I looked at yuenx, MakeUseOf, Offgridweb and a web search and found no named lab or reviewer measurement.
Rivals' 12V car-port wattage (Jackery 1500 v2, DELTA 2 Max): their store pages returned 429, so the 12V Anderson output cannot be shown to beat named rivals.
Battery cycles, capacity and price of the new Yeti 1500: the full product page returned 429. Store search text gave the price, 5-year warranty, weight and inputs, but the battery section was cut off.
Digital Camera World review: the page body did not load. Manuals.plus and REI returned 403.
